state.misconception_label: Does not know the properties of a rectangle

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. The angle on the right hand side at the centre is highlighted in red and the angle at the bottom at the centre is highlighted in yellow.](). I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a rectangular piece of paper and you fold it along its diagonals. What do you notice about the angles where the diagonals intersect? This real-world scenario can help us understand why the angles in a rectangle are not always equal.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see what you mean - when I fold the paper along the diagonals, the angles where they cross in the middle aren't all the same size. So some of them are bigger and some are smaller, right? But I'm still confused about which angles can never be acute - does that mean they have to be obtuse or something?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a rectangular piece of paper and you fold it along its intersecting diagonals. What do you notice about the angles where the diagonals intersect? This real-world scenario can help us understand why the angles in a rectangle are not always equal. Remember, the angles on a rectangle can never be acute because of this specific property.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, so you're saying the angles *of* the rectangle itself can never be acute? But I thought all rectangles have 90-degree angles at the corners... Oh! Do you mean the angles made where the diagonals cross in the middle? Because those are the ones that change depending on the rectangle's shape, right?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses a generic folding activity that doesn't directly address the student's confusion about angles at diagonal intersections, makes an inaccurate claim that rectangle corner angles can never be acute (they're always 90°), but the student does eventually self-correct to distinguish between corner angles and diagonal intersection angles.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses a concrete, hands-on analogy (folding a rectangular piece of paper along diagonals) to help the student visualize and understand the abstract geometric concept of diagonal intersection angles, which is a strong application of the experiential strategy.
